direction_note: Cycle 6: scrapped carry_cross_weekend_premium with a lesson (no weekend or weekday-overnight premium in AUDJPY net of costs; all 16 arms negative in design, check flat; do not retry with other hours, the short side, EURJPY/GBPJPY, a vol gate or an equity aux). Registered one hypothesis, chosen as the last unused dimension of the data store: fx_liquidity_withdrawal_reversal, fade a large one-hour move on USDJPY M15 only when the quoted spread widened to at least twice its slot median during the move, with a no-spread-condition control, a scheduled-news control and a one-bar entry delay in the stage A grid. Critic: revise (control must be ratio 0 because spreads are quantised; rollover always excluded; per-leg news blocks for stage B; two grids so a 2,000-trade control cannot carry stages B and C; hypothesis-cell floor with date-clustered t; fix-flow rule; pooled seven-market replication; counts and costs restated), amended in full before any run. Build: checker ok first time; code review found one real blocker (float ties at the 2x threshold dropped 37 of 106 exact-tie bars), fixed with a 1e-9 relative tolerance, counts corrected before any run (160 episodes on 123 trading days), second review approve. Result: killed at stage A on USDJPY; the best of 16 cells by t was the news-included control at -0.004 R. Pre-registered diagnostics (runs/fx_liquidity_withdrawal_reversal/posthoc.md): hypothesis cell 160 design episodes, gross R exactly 0.000 and net -0.020 R (t -0.31, date-clustered t +0.22; check -0.065 R on 97), fill spread 0.89 pips, stop exits 22 percent with a mean overshoot of 0.66 R beyond the stop (gap exposure in thin markets); delay-1 arm -0.058 R; move 0.40 x ATR cells -0.078 and -0.107 R. The plain hourly shock fade control lost -0.068 R (t -4.5, 2,075 episodes; gross -0.039 R), so one-hour moves of at least 0.25 x ATR20 on USDJPY continue by about 4 percent of their size over the next two hours before costs; the spread condition removes that continuation but produces no reversal (rule 2 difference +0.048 R, below the +0.08 R bar, and the arm itself is negative). The news-included arm (-0.004 R net, +0.020 R gross) reverted slightly more than the non-news arm, the opposite of the mechanism's prediction. Pooled over the seven other markets the hypothesis cell made -0.051 R in design (300 episodes, clustered t 0.05) and -0.018 R in check (209). Fix-window episodes (14) change nothing. One post-hoc slice (28 episodes whose window held the 23:50 UTC Japan releases or the 06:30 BoJ press conference, +0.47 R) is a snooped subset and must not be registered. LESSON FOR THE SCRAP INDEX (to be recorded as cycle 7's judgment): liquidity withdrawal measured by the quoted spread does not create a tradeable reversal in FX; the mean two-hour retracement of a large one-hour move made under a 2x spread blow-out is zero before costs on USDJPY and negative pooled across seven other markets, while the unconditional fade loses -0.07 R. Do not retry with other spread thresholds (3x had 31 episodes), other move sizes, M5 or H1 bars, limit entries, a longer or shorter hold, a different stage A market, or the 'continuation when spreads are wide' mirror (its sign would be read off this run). With this, every state variable in the data store has been used as a trigger (clock, calendar, level, size, volume, spread, cross-market shocks) and the liquidity-provision family joins the dead pile. PROGRAMME ASSESSMENT for the user: six cycles have tested eight mechanisms (three rejected before compute, five killed at stage A with controls in place) on top of the 171-test alpha hunt, the 600,912-cell flow atlas and the pattern searches; nothing new has reached stage B, and the price-spread-and-clock hypothesis space reachable with Dukascopy bars is exhausted for FX, gold and the two index CFDs with data. Further cycles without new inputs would mostly produce more honest negatives. Options: (a) pause the loop; (b) add external inputs that open new families (a scheduled-event calendar with surprise sizes, retail positioning ratios, options risk reversals and implied vol, the FX swap basis, CFTC at daily resolution); (c) redirect effort to the sizing and risk design of the existing USDJPY basket (prop_sim and prop_risk_rules in gj-strat), which is a simulation task, not a hypothesis. ENGINE NOTES: thresholds on quantised quantities need tie-safe comparisons (relative 1e-9) or the sample depends on floating-point noise and changes under widen_spread; stage A ranks all cells by t, so control arms with many trades must be confined to spec stage_a.grid while spec grid holds the hypothesis arm only; the report prints 15 of 16 stage A rows, the rest is in the trials table.

judgments.lesson: There is no weekend risk premium in carry crosses net of costs, and no weekday-overnight premium either. On AUDJPY every one of the 16 pre-registered arms lost in design (2010-2017, 412 trades per arm): the eight Friday-to-Monday arms made -0.008 to -0.030 R (t -1.2 to -2.5) and the eight Monday-to-Tuesday overnight controls -0.004 to -0.026 R (t -0.3 to -4.3); the check period was flat (-0.021 to +0.006 R). Holding AUDJPY across the Friday-to-Monday gap costs the weekend-edge spread (3-4 pips round trip including commission) and earns nothing in price; the premium that equities show overnight does not exist in FX carry pairs at this horizon. Stage B never ran, so NZDJPY, AUDUSD, NZDUSD and EURJPY are unmeasured, but the primary market was the best-motivated one and the control arms lost too. Do not retry with other entry or exit hours, the Thursday-to-Monday hold, the short side (a snooped flip), EURJPY or GBPJPY stage A, a VIX or realised-vol gate, or an equity-state aux condition.
judgments.notes: Killed at GA_stage_a_floor on AUDJPY. The design worked as intended: the control arm was in the grid, the exit and cost rules were fixed before the run after the Critic's revisions, and the negative is unambiguous. This was the first adequately powered test in three cycles (412 design trades per arm) and it closes the weekend-hold horizon for FX in this programme.

hypotheses.title: Liquidity-withdrawal reversal: fade a large one-hour move only when the quoted spread blew out during it (dealers withdrew), with no-spread-condition and scheduled-news control arms, on USDJPY first
hypotheses.rationale: Mechanism (Nagel 2012, 'Evaporating liquidity'; Brunnermeier and Pedersen 2009; Mancini, Ranaldo and Wrampelmeyer 2013 for FX): short-term price reversals are the compensation liquidity providers earn for absorbing order imbalances, and that compensation is large only when liquidity supply is scarce. In FX the scarcity is observable: when dealers and ECN liquidity providers pull or widen their quotes, the top-of-book spread widens several-fold against its normal level at that time of day. A large move that happens while quotes are withdrawn is, in part, a price concession paid by an impatient liquidity demander (a stop cascade, a forced hedger, a margin-driven seller) to the few providers still quoting; once quoting resumes, the concession is competed away and the price retraces. The same-sized move made with normal, tight quotes is information being priced by a deep book and should not retrace; this is what every prior fade in this programme measured, and they all lost (session reversal, Asian-extreme fade, quiet-hours Bollinger fade, sweep fades, one-day shock fade -0.10 R on EURUSD). Those tests conditioned on clock, level or size, never on the state of liquidity supply, so their negatives are consistent with this hypothesis rather than against it; the tick-volume test (fx_volume_climax_reversal) tried to measure liquidity demand with a quantity that does not measure it, and its lesson forbids volume, not spread. The quoted spread is the one data dimension in this store that no prior test has used as a signal input. Design: bars M15 on USDJPY (0.6 pip median spread, the classic liquidity-gap currency; the 2010-05-06, 2011-03-17, 2013-05-23, 2015-08-24 and 2016-06-24 episodes are in the design years). The state is the bar's quoted-spread proxy relative to the median of the same 15-minute slot over its previous 20 occurrences, so the daily spread profile and the rollover widening cancel out; the trigger is a one-hour mid-price move of at least 0.25 or 0.40 x ATR20. Two controls sit in the grid: spread_ratio_min = 1 (no spread condition; the plain intraday shock fade, which the mechanism predicts to be about zero or negative) and exclude_news = false (keeps moves inside the three scheduled-announcement blocks, 12:00-15:30, 18:00-20:00 and 03:00-05:00 UTC, plus the 20:45-22:15 rollover; these are information-driven and the mechanism predicts no reversal there, which the NFP fade result of -0.12 R already suggests). The hypothesis arm is spread_ratio_min >= 2 with exclude_news = true. Market-fact counts from the design years (counts only, no outcomes): USDJPY M15 bars with spread ratio >= 2 and a one-hour move >= 0.25 x ATR20 number about 920, of which about 55 percent sit inside the news blocks; outside the blocks there are roughly 370 bars forming about 230 distinct episodes (29 per year), and about 230 episodes on EURUSD; the ratio >= 3 arm has only about 65 non-news episodes and is a surface point, not the primary. Costs are the real threat and are accepted up front: the fill right after a liquidity event pays whatever spread is quoted at the next open, so a 17-pip move (0.25 x ATR20) faded at a 1.5-2 pip spread plus 0.2 pip slippage plus about 0.8 pip commission costs 0.13-0.18 R, and the entry_delay_bars = 1 arm (order placed one bar later, after quotes normally refill) measures how much of the retracement survives waiting 15 minutes for a cheaper fill. Every arm must report the mean entry spread so the cost question is answered in the open. Expected: the hypothesis arm retraces 25-40 percent of the move within two hours on average (+0.25 to +0.40 R gross), net +0.08 R after costs with sd about 0.6 R, so with 230 trades design t is about 1.5-2.5; the control arm should be at or below zero. Human execution: a prop trader with a spread alert on the platform can take this (one order, a stop at the move size, a two-hour time exit); it is not a scalp.
hypotheses.rules:
All times UTC. Bars: M15, labelled by open time; a bar's close time is ts + 15 minutes. Bars are sparse; locate by timestamp and never assume one bar per slot.

DEFINITIONS (all computed from closed bars 0..i):
- mid_c[i] = (bid_c[i] + ask_c[i]) / 2. The one-hour move ending at bar i is move[i] = mid_c[i] - mid_c[i-4]; require i >= 4 and ts[i] - ts[i-4] <= 75 minutes, otherwise no signal at i.
- ATR20[i] = F.atr_prev(F.daily_bars(m), 20) mapped to bars (known at the start of the trading day); require finite and > 0.
- Quoted-spread proxy of bar i: spr[i] = max(ask_o[i] - bid_o[i], ask_c[i] - bid_c[i], ask_h[i] - bid_h[i], ask_l[i] - bid_l[i]) (price units).
- Slot of bar i: slot[i] = F.minute_of_day_utc(m)[i] (0..1425 in steps of 15). norm[i] = median of spr over the previous 20 bars that share slot[i], strictly before bar i (not including i); require 20 such bars exist and norm[i] > 0, otherwise no signal at i. ratio[i] = spr[i] / norm[i].
- News blocks (UTC, half-open): [03:00, 05:00), [12:00, 15:30), [18:00, 20:00), [20:45, 22:15). The move window of bar i is [ts[i] + 15 min - 60 min, ts[i] + 15 min). When exclude_news is true, no signal at i if the move window overlaps any block (compare minute-of-day of the window start and end against each block; all blocks lie inside one UTC day).

SIGNAL CONDITION at bar i: |move[i]| >= move_atr_min * ATR20[i] AND ratio[i] >= spread_ratio_min AND (exclude_news is false OR the move window is outside all blocks). spread_ratio_min = 1 is the no-spread-condition control arm (ratio >= 1 is always true wherever norm is defined).

ONE TRADE PER EPISODE: scan candidate bars in ascending order; accept bar i only if i >= last_accepted + cooldown_bars (cooldown_bars = 12, i.e. three hours), where last_accepted is the last accepted signal bar; set last_accepted = i on acceptance.

ORDER PLACEMENT: let j = i + entry_delay_bars (entry_delay_bars 0 or 1); require j < m.n and, when entry_delay_bars = 1, ts[j] - ts[i] <= 30 minutes (otherwise skip the episode). All signal fields are written at index j and use only information from bars <= j (the condition was decided at i <= j).
- If move[i] > 0: entry_short[j] = True (fade an up move). If move[i] < 0: entry_long[j] = True (fade a down move).
- entry_type[j] = 0 (market at the open of bar j + 1, ask for longs, bid for shorts), valid_bars[j] = 1.
- sl_dist[j] = stop_mult * |move[i]| with stop_mult = 1.0 (so 1 R = the size of the move being faded); always > 0 because |move[i]| >= move_atr_min * ATR20 > 0.
- tp_dist[j] = NaN (no target; the time exit measures the mean retracement).
- max_bars[j] = hold_bars = 8 (close at the open of the bar after holding eight M15 bars, about two hours).
- No exit_long / exit_short signals; no other filters; no pyramiding (the executor blocks entries while a position is open).

PARAMETERS: spread_ratio_min (grid 1, 2, 3), move_atr_min (grid 0.25, 0.40), exclude_news (grid true, false), entry_delay_bars (grid 0, 1); fixed: stop_mult 1.0, hold_bars 8, cooldown_bars 12, norm_window 20, max_gap_min 75. Every one of these is read from p.

REPORTING (stage A table and stage C): for every arm report the number of episodes, avg R, t, the mean quoted spread at the fill bar's open in pips, and gross R before spread and commission; report design years individually.

pre_registered.kill_if: (1) Stage A floor on USDJPY applies to the hypothesis arms only: if the best combination in design is a control arm (spread_ratio_min = 1 or exclude_news = false) the hypothesis is dead regardless of its numbers, because then the reversal, if any, is not a liquidity effect; among the hypothesis arms (spread_ratio_min >= 2 and exclude_news = true) the best must have design avg R > 0 and t >= 1 with at least 150 episodes. (2) Control: at the chosen move_atr_min and entry_delay_bars, avg R(spread_ratio_min = 2, exclude_news = true) minus avg R(spread_ratio_min = 1, exclude_news = true) must be >= +0.08 R in design; if the plain intraday shock fade earns as much, the spread adds nothing and the hypothesis dies. (3) Information control: at the chosen arm, the news version (exclude_news = false) must not beat the non-news version by more than 0.05 R in design; if moves inside the scheduled-announcement blocks revert more, the effect is overreaction to news, not liquidity provision, and the liquidity label is scrapped with that lesson. (4) Costs: the hard gate (positive at 1.5x costs) stands; the mean fill spread per arm is reported, and if the entry_delay_bars = 0 arm is positive gross but negative net while the delay = 1 arm is also negative, the lesson is that the concession is real but belongs to the liquidity providers who are already quoting, not to a market-order taker. (5) Regime: at least half of the design years positive at the chosen arm. (6) Stage B: the chosen arm must be positive in design on at least 3 of the 8 markets, and the pooled check must be positive with at least 30 trades (hard gate). Honest expectation: about 230 non-news episodes on USDJPY in design, net +0.08 R, design t 1.5-2.5; the ratio >= 3 arm (about 65 episodes) is underpowered and is a surface point, not a primary; the most likely failure is cost, because the fade is entered at a spread that is still wide.

hypotheses.why_different: Every prior fade in the index conditioned on the clock (session reversal, Tokyo-open contrarian, quiet-hours Bollinger fade, night scalp), on a price level (sweeps of the previous session's extreme, round numbers, Asian-range fade), on the size of a one-day move (shock fade, z-score fade) or on tick volume (volume climax); none conditioned on the state of liquidity supply, and none measured the quoted spread at all. This hypothesis uses the spread as the state variable, works at the intraday episode horizon (one-hour moves on M15 bars) rather than the session or day, and carries its own falsification structure: a no-spread-condition arm that reproduces the known negative baseline inside the same design, and a scheduled-news arm that the mechanism predicts to be worse. The tick-volume lesson forbids volume as an input and the follow-the-shock mirror; neither is used here. The NFP fade (edge_hunt) faded a single scheduled release at a fixed clock time, which is exactly the information-driven case this design puts in the control arm.

director.direction_note: Cycle 6 scraps the weekend-premium test with a lesson (no weekend or weekday-overnight premium in AUDJPY net of costs; all 16 arms negative in design, check flat) and registers one hypothesis, chosen because it is the last unused dimension of this data store: the quoted spread as a measure of liquidity supply. Before choosing it I checked the remaining candidates against the reports: the full close-to-open index overnight premium was already measured (index_anomalies E2a/E2b on Nasdaq, design -0.03 to -0.05 R, check negative) and the European-open version died on costs; the atlas scanned every clock window on all weekdays plus Wednesday/Thursday, gotobi, holiday-adjacent and k-th-weekday day types, so no new calendar idea can clear its t >= 3.7 bar; cross-sectional 'idiosyncratic' cross moves do not exist in FX because triangular consistency makes every pair return an exact difference of currency factors; XAGUSD, GER40, UK100, US30 are not in the data store, USA500 ends 2025-05, and JP225 has no Tokyo-morning bars in 2015-2017. The liquidity-state test has about 230 non-news episodes on USDJPY in design, carries its own controls (no-spread-condition arm, scheduled-news arm, one-bar entry delay for the cost question) and will most likely fail on the fill spread; if it fails, the liquidity-provision family is closed for good and the honest statement to the user stands: with price, spread and clock data alone the hypothesis space reachable here is exhausted after six cycles and the gj-strat scans before them. The next useful inputs are external: a scheduled-event calendar with surprise sizes, retail positioning (the broker long/short ratios), options risk reversals and implied vol, and the FX swap basis; without them the remaining lever for the Alpha Swing pass probability is the sizing and risk design of the USDJPY basket, which is a simulation task, not a hypothesis. Engine notes for later cycles: the M15 feed has about 195,000 design bars per major; the same-slot spread median needs 20 prior occurrences, so the first month of 2010 is unusable; the Builder must use mid prices for the move so a spread blow-out alone cannot register as a bid-side move.

reasons: This deserves compute and is not a duplicate. The quoted spread has never been used as a liquidity-state signal in this programme. The only earlier use is entry spread as one feature inside the box_meta logistic filter. Nagel's evaporating-liquidity argument is a real economic mechanism. The volume-climax lesson forbids volume, not spread. The horizon here (a one-hour move and a two-hour hold) is not the one-day shock fade that was scrapped. The prior is against plain intraday reversal on USDJPY. Its H1 AC1 is about 0. The quiet-hours Bollinger fade made -0.062 R (t -3.4). After 3292 USDJPY box stop-outs (gj-strat after_sl), price kept going the stop way on average: +0.08 R at 30 min, +0.11 R at 1 h. So any edge must come from the spread condition alone. The control arms test exactly that, and a clean negative would close the last unused dimension of this data store.

The control arm is wrong as written. The rules say 'ratio >= 1 is always true wherever norm is defined'. That is false: ratio is the bar's spread over its own slot median, so roughly half of all bars are below 1. I counted USDJPY M15 design bars, 2010-2017, using counts and spreads only and no returns. Of the 11,267 bars with a one-hour move >= 0.25 x ATR20, 28.9% have ratio < 1 and 27.9% have ratio exactly 1, because spreads are quantised at 0.1 pip. So spread_ratio_min = 1 is a 'spread at or above its median' arm. It is not the no-condition baseline that kill rule (2) needs.

The grid does not fit the pipeline. Stages A and B pick the best cell by design t over the whole grid. The walk-forward re-optimises over the whole grid. A promotion runs the holdout on whatever cells stage C chose. The no-spread control has about 15 times the trades of the hypothesis arm on USDJPY: 2,075 versus 135 non-news episodes at k = 0.25. Any small positive mean therefore gives the control the larger t. Stages B and C, the hard gates and a promotion would then all be testing a control arm. Kill rule (1), dead 'if the best combination in design is a control arm', has the same bias: a +0.01 R control with 2,000 trades outranks a +0.08 R hypothesis arm with 135.

The sample is about 40% smaller than registered. Under the rules as written, the whole one-hour move window must avoid the blocks. USDJPY design has 938 bars with ratio >= 2 and a move >= 0.25 x ATR20. Of these, 670 (71%) lie in or touch a block, not 55%. The other 268 bars form 135 episodes on 105 distinct dates, not about 230. k = 0.40 gives 76 episodes, and ratio >= 3 gives 31 (k = 0.25) and 22 (k = 0.40). EURUSD gives 146, not about 230. The registered minimum of 150 trades cannot be met. At +0.08 R with sd 0.6-0.7, the expected design t is about 1.2-1.5, and lower once trades are grouped by date. Stage A on USDJPY therefore has only about a 60% chance of passing even if the effect is real.

Costs are smaller than registered, and waiting does not buy a cheaper fill. In the hypothesis arm the spread at the next open averages 0.90 pips (median 0.70, p90 1.60). At entry_delay_bars = 1 it averages 0.83. The spread condition selects large moves: median |move| is 39.7 pips (p10 22.7). The round trip is about 1.8-1.9 pips: half the spread on entry and exit, 0.4 pip of slippage and about 0.7 pip of commission. That is about 0.05 R on average, about 0.08 R at the p10 move, and about 0.10 R at 2x costs. The registered '0.13-0.18 R' does not match these numbers. The registered 'gross +0.25 to +0.40 R, net +0.08 R' is not internally consistent either. The delay arm measures how fast the reversion happens and how much execution latency costs; it does not measure a cheaper fill. On the other stage B markets costs are about 0.04-0.08 R. GBPJPY and AUDJPY fills average 5.9 and 4.5 pips after a flag.

The news blocks are built around USD and JPY. In stage B they leave each other currency's scheduled releases inside the 'liquidity' arm. I applied the US blocks to every market and added each leg's own release windows: EUR/GBP data 06:00-10:15 UTC, the summer BoE/ECB decisions in 10:45-12:00 UTC, Australian data plus China data and the PBoC fix in 00:15-02:15 UTC, and the RBA in 03:00-05:00 UTC. Design episodes then fall as follows: GBPUSD 274 -> 33, AUDUSD 165 -> 20, EURUSD 146 -> 57, EURJPY 119 -> 40, GBPJPY 223 -> 36, AUDJPY 163 -> 17. XAUUSD has 82. So outside USDJPY, 'spread blow-out during a big move' mostly marks scheduled releases. Stage B as written would mainly test reversal after news, which the hypothesis's own mechanism says should not happen. With proper blocks, stage B is a thin replication of about 285 episodes over seven markets. The '3 of 8 markets positive' rule then has almost no power: at 17-82 trades per market, most markets come out positive about half the time even with no edge.

The motivating episodes are not in the tested arm. 2011-03-16/17 and 2013-05-23 contribute no hypothesis-arm episodes. On 2010-05-06, 14 of the 16 flagged bars fall in the blocks, and the only hypothesis episode is at 23:30 UTC. 2015-08-24 contributes 4 and 2016-06-24 contributes 3. In the typical hypothesis-arm 'withdrawal' the spread widens from a 0.5-pip slot median to about 1.3 pips (median ratio 2.25). I checked against M1 data: in 70% of the flagged bars, an M1 open or close quote inside the bar was at least 2x the norm. So the max-of-four proxy mostly reflects real quotes, and the remaining 30% come from the high/low spreads alone. In practice the arm tests mild, frequent widening in fast markets rather than dealers pulling out. That is acceptable as an operational definition, but the rationale should say so.

Overfit risk is medium. The threat is concentration more than search. After revision the grid is small, set from theory, and contains its own controls. But the 135 USDJPY episodes fall on only 105 dates. Nineteen dates hold 49 of them: 9 on 2015-08-24/25, 4 on US election night 2016-11-09, and 3 each on 2015-08-21, 2013-06-11 (a BoJ day), 2016-06-24 and 2010-05-07. The years 2015-2016 alone hold 60. In stage B, using the proposer's blocks, 408 of 1,225 market-episodes fall on dates shared by 3 or more markets. Trade-level t-statistics overstate the evidence in both cases. There is a small overlap with fix flows: 6 episodes have the winter 16:00 UTC WM/R fix inside the move window, and 6 have the 00:55 UTC Tokyo fix on a gotobi day. Both families have already been measured (prior_fix_fades, gotobi short).

Live execution may not match the test. The trigger is defined on Dukascopy's quote feed. A prop-firm feed widens its spread on its own schedule (markups, rollover, news), so live triggers will differ unless the signal is computed from a Dukascopy feed and the order is placed on the prop account. The setup fires about 17 times a year at unpredictable hours, 44% of them between 23:00 and 03:00 UTC, so it needs an EA. The executor fills intrabar stops at the stop level plus 0.2 pip. That is optimistic in exactly the thin markets this strategy trades. With a median stop of about 40 pips the expected bias is small (about 0.01-0.02 R), but the tail is not small.
reviews.revisions: 1) Control arm. Use spread_ratio_min = 0 as the no-spread-condition control. Keep the rule that norm must be defined, so every arm covers the same period. Delete 'ratio >= 1 is always true'. Drop spread_ratio_min = 3: it has 31 and 22 design episodes and cannot be read. 2) Rollover. Always exclude moves whose window touches [20:45, 22:15) UTC, in every arm. This is a data-quality exclusion (asymmetric spread widening distorts the mid price), not news. exclude_news switches only the scheduled-release blocks. This changes the USDJPY news-inclusive arm from 544 to 522 episodes and leaves the hypothesis arm at 135. 3) News blocks per market. Times are fixed UTC and half-open, and the move-window overlap test stays as written, including windows that cross 00:00 UTC. Apply [12:00, 15:30) and [18:00, 20:00) to every market. Add each leg's own blocks: JPY [03:00, 05:00); EUR [06:00, 10:15) and [11:30, 12:00); GBP [06:00, 10:15) and [10:45, 12:00); AUD [00:15, 02:15) and [03:00, 05:00); USD and XAU get none of their own. USDJPY keeps exactly its four registered blocks. 4) Two grids. The Director should set them in specs/auto/fx_liquidity_withdrawal_reversal.json after 'cycle_step.py review' and before 'test'. Stage A: stage_a = {"market": "USDJPY", "grid": {"spread_ratio_min": [0, 2], "exclude_news": [true, false], "move_atr_min": [0.25, 0.4], "entry_delay_bars": [0, 1]}}. These 16 cells are the only place the controls run. Stages B, C, the walk-forward and any holdout use spec grid = {"spread_ratio_min": [2], "exclude_news": [true], "move_atr_min": [0.25], "entry_delay_bars": [0, 1]} (2 cells). The registered hypothesis grid may stay at the 16 cells so the checker exercises every value. The report keeps only the top 15 stage A rows, so read all 16 from the trials table (stage 'A'). 5) Kill rules. Replace (1) with: on USDJPY, the hypothesis cell (ratio 2, non-news, k 0.25, at whichever delay has the higher design t) must have design avg R > 0, trade-level t >= 1 and date-clustered t >= 1 (R averaged per 17:00-New-York trading day), with at least 120 episodes. The automatic stage A gate ranks all 16 cells by t and does not replace this check. If the hypothesis cell fails, scrap even if the pipeline reports a candidate. Delete 'dead if the best combination is a control arm'. Keep (2) at +0.08 R, now measured against spread_ratio_min = 0 at the same k, delay and exclude_news = true. Keep (3) at 0.05 R, comparing news-inclusive with non-news at ratio 2, with the rollover excluded in both. Keep (4) and (5). Add a fix-flow rule: design avg R at the chosen cell must stay > 0 after removing episodes whose move window contains 16:00 UTC in UK winter (the WM/R fix) or 00:55 UTC on a gotobi day. If it does not, the effect is fix flow, which has already been measured, and the hypothesis is dead. Replace the '3 of 8 markets positive' part of (6) with an out-of-market replication: at the hypothesis cell, design avg R pooled over the seven non-primary markets must be > 0. Report its date-clustered t, and report pooled check and walk-forward statistics date-clustered across markets as well. Keep the pooled-check hard gate. 6) Restate counts and expectations. USDJPY design has 135 episodes on 105 dates at k 0.25, and 76 at k 0.40; the k 0.40 cells are a stage-A surface point only. Stage B with per-leg blocks: EURUSD 57, GBPUSD 33, AUDUSD 20, EURJPY 40, GBPJPY 36, AUDJPY 17, XAUUSD 82. AUDUSD and AUDJPY fall under the pipeline's 30-trade floor, so they enter only the pooled replication. Set min_trades_design_per_market = 120 for USDJPY and expected design t = 1.2-1.5. State that if the true effect is +0.08 R, a stage A kill has roughly a 35-40% chance of being a false negative, so a kill is weak evidence and a pass is strong evidence. 7) Restate costs. The fill spread is 0.90 pips at delay 0 and 0.83 at delay 1, and the median |move| is 40 pips. All-in cost is about 0.05 R on USDJPY, 0.04-0.08 R on the stage B markets, and about 0.10 R on USDJPY at 2x costs. Make gross and net agree: a net of +0.08 R needs a gross of about +0.13 R, which is a mean retracement of about 13% of the move, not 25-40%. Describe entry_delay_bars as a latency and timing check, not a way to get a cheaper fill. 8) Stage C reports, all computed from the trades. (a) The share of trades that exit at the stop, and the mean of (mae_r - 1) on those exits, to show gap exposure. (b) Avg R without the 5 trading days with the largest total R. Removing the best 5 of about 105 days costs about 0.05-0.07 R by construction even if the effect is real, so treat this as a diagnostic, not a gate. (c) Episodes whose move window contains the 23:50 UTC Japan releases or the 06:30 UTC BoJ press conference, reported separately. 9) Rationale. Remove the claim that the 2010-05-06, 2011-03-17 and 2013-05-23 episodes are tested. Describe the arm as measured: the spread widens from about 0.5 to 1.3 pips during a large one-hour move outside the scheduled windows.
reviews.notes_for_builder: Implement exactly these definitions; I counted with them. (1) Spread proxy: spr = max(ask_o-bid_o, ask_c-bid_c, ask_h-bid_h, ask_l-bid_l) per bar. The loader already clamps ask >= bid. (2) Slot norm: slot = F.minute_of_day_utc(m). Loop over the 96 slots, never over bars. For a slot with ascending bar indices idx, set norm[idx[k]] = median(spr[idx[k-W:k]]) for k >= W, where W = p['norm_window'], and NaN otherwise. It must be strictly before the bar: use numpy.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view(x, W), take the median over axis 1, and assign window r to idx[r+W]. ratio = spr / norm, used only where norm is finite and > 0. (3) Move and ATR: mid = (bid_c + ask_c) / 2; move[i] = mid[i] - mid[i-4], valid only if i >= 4 and ts[i] - ts[i-4] <= p['max_gap_min'] minutes. ATR comes from daily = F.daily_bars(m); atr = daily.to_bars(F.atr_prev(daily, 20)), which must be finite and > 0. (4) Window overlap: let mod be the bar's open minute of day. ws = (mod - 45) % 1440 and we = (mod + 15) % 1440. For a block [b0, b1): if ws < we, it overlaps when ws < b1 and b0 < we. If ws >= we, the window crosses 00:00 UTC (this includes we == 0), and it overlaps when ws < b1 or b0 < we. (5) Blocks in minutes. ROLL = [(1245, 1335)], always applied. NEWS = US [(720, 930), (1080, 1200)] plus the leg blocks for m.sym[:3] and m.sym[3:6]: JPY [(180, 300)], EUR [(360, 615), (690, 720)], GBP [(360, 615), (645, 720)], AUD [(15, 135), (180, 300)], USD and XAU []. NEWS is applied only when exclude_news is true. (6) Candidate bar: valid move, valid atr and norm, |move| >= move_atr_min * atr, ratio >= spread_ratio_min, no ROLL overlap, and (not exclude_news or no NEWS overlap). (7) Episodes: loop over candidate indices only. Accept i if i >= last + cooldown_bars, and set last = i at acceptance, BEFORE the delay checks, so both delays use the same episode set. Then j = i + entry_delay_bars. Skip if j >= m.n, or if entry_delay_bars > 0 and ts[j] - ts[i] > p['delay_max_gap_min'] (30) minutes. (8) Orders, written at index j: entry_short if move[i] > 0, else entry_long; entry_type 0; valid_bars 1; sl_dist = stop_mult * |move[i]|; tp_dist NaN; max_bars = hold_bars. Never read ts[j+1] or any field of the fill bar; that is look-ahead. (9) PARAMS: spread_ratio_min 2, move_atr_min 0.25, exclude_news True, entry_delay_bars 0, stop_mult 1.0, hold_bars 8, cooldown_bars 12, norm_window 20, max_gap_min 75, delay_max_gap_min 30. Module GRID = the 16-cell stage A grid: spread_ratio_min [0, 2], exclude_news [True, False], move_atr_min [0.25, 0.4], entry_delay_bars [0, 1]. (10) Sanity counts for signal bars on USDJPY M15, 2010-2017 only: defaults about 135; spread_ratio_min 0 about 2,075; exclude_news False (rollover still excluded) about 522; move_atr_min 0.4 about 76. EURUSD defaults about 57 with the EUR blocks. If your counts differ by more than about 10%, recheck the window-overlap and slot-median logic before anything else.
